summary:
CosmoSPHERE is an interactive web platform that transforms real observations from NASA's SPHEREx space telescope into an accessible exploration of the infrared sky across time and wavelength.
SPHEREx collects an extraordinary amount of scientific information about the universe, but interpreting multidimensional astronomical observations can be challenging for students, educators, and people without specialized training.
Our solution allows users to explore celestial objects through an interactive sky map or astronomical coordinates, visualize observations from different epochs, and investigate infrared spectra across six SPHEREx detector bands covering approximately 0.75–5.0 micrometers.
CosmoSPHERE retrieves authentic observations from NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), processes astronomical FITS images, aligns observations onto a common celestial grid, generates scientifically grounded false-color visualizations, and extracts spectral measurements through multi-epoch photometry.
An interactive timeline helps users explore different observation periods, while spectral charts reveal the infrared characteristics of selected celestial targets. Preprocessed observations of selected objects provide a faster exploration experience.
By combining real NASA data, scientific computing, and interactive visualization, CosmoSPHERE makes infrared astronomy more approachable and encourages scientific curiosity, education, and exploration.
details:
CosmoSPHERE is an interactive scientific exploration platform that transforms real observations from NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope into accessible, visually engaging experiences. The platform combines an interactive frontend with a scientific processing backend. When users select astronomical coordinates or a target, the backend queries the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), retrieves specific FITS image regions, spatially aligns observations onto a common celestial grid, normalizes infrared measurements into false-color image layers across six detector bands, organizes them into chronological temporal sequences, and performs multi-epoch forced photometry for spectral analysis.

The benefits provided by CosmoSPHERE are:

  • Educational Accessibility: Helps students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts explore real infrared observations through an approachable interface.
  • Scientific Literacy: Encourages users to understand how astronomical observations are collected, processed, and interpreted.
  • Multidimensional Understanding: Combines spatial, temporal, and spectral information to investigate targets from unique perspectives.
  • Efficient Data Processing: Utilizes targeted data retrieval, asynchronous computation, and caching to minimize unnecessary processing.
  • Open-Source Development: Supports transparency, technical learning, and future collaboration.

The primary objective is to reduce barriers between advanced astronomical research data and the public. By making authentic NASA observations approachable in a web-based environment, the project aims to inspire educational demonstrations, independent learning, astronomy outreach, and introductory scientific investigation, demonstrating how open data and software engineering can make the universe more accessible.

The tools the we used to develop the system were, for each topic:

  • Frontend Development: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, CSS Modules, WebGL, Aladin Lite, and Plotly.js.
  • Backend Development: Node.js, Express, Python, FastAPI, and Pydantic.
  • Scientific Computing & Data: Astropy, Astroquery, PyVO, NumPy, SciPy, Reproject, Pillow, FITS processing, WCS transformations, and multi-epoch photometric analysis.
  • Data Sources: NASA SPHEREx mission observations and NASA/IPAC IRSA services.
  • Infrastructure & Deployment: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Docker, Docker Compose, Traefik, Portainer, Cloudflare, GitHub Actions, Git, and GitHub. (No specialized physical hardware is required beyond a modern web browser and internet connection).

CosmoSPHERE’s creativity lies in transforming complex, multidimensional astronomical datasets into an intuitive, interactive exploration experience. Instead of presenting observations solely as static files or numerical tables, it integrates spatial, temporal, and spectral exploration into a single environment, translating invisible infrared wavelengths into meaningful false-color representations without requiring specialized software.

The factors that we considered for this project were:

  • Scientific Integrity: Ensuring the use of authentic NASA data with a clear distinction between measured information and false-color visualization.
  • Accuracy and Comparability: Implementing consistent celestial grids, image reprojection, and controlled normalization for multi-epoch comparisons.
  • Performance and Scalability: Utilizing targeted data retrieval, caching, and asynchronous processing to handle large datasets.
  • Accessibility and User Experience: Designing intuitive navigation and controls that do not require advanced programming knowledge.
  • Transparency and Reproducibility: Providing open-source code, technical documentation, and clear API contracts.
  • Scientific Limitations: Acknowledging that the implementation is primarily for exploration and educational visualization, thereby communicating results responsibly.
